explanation.why: 30 large and 30 small shirts make 60 shirts for 30(18) + 30(12) = $900. With 31 large and 29 small the cost is $906, which is over budget.
explanation.pattern: With a minimum count and a maximum budget, push the cheaper item to its minimum and substitute into the budget inequality.

items.stem: The system of inequalities \(x \ge 2a - 3\) and \(x < 4a - 11\) has no solution for \(x\). If \(a\) is a positive integer, how many possible values of \(a\) are there?

steps: There is no solution exactly when the lower bound is greater than or equal to the upper bound.
Write that inequality in a and simplify.
Count the positive integers that satisfy it.
explanation.why: 2a - 3 \ge 4a - 11 gives a \le 4, so a = 1, 2, 3, 4.
explanation.pattern: A system of one-sided bounds on x has no solution when the lower bound reaches the upper bound; solve that for the parameter.

items.stem: A caterer buys trays of sandwiches for $14 each and trays of salads for $22 each, and spends no more than $600 in total. The number of sandwich trays is at least 3 more than 2 times the number of salad trays. What is the greatest number of salad trays the caterer can buy?

steps: Let s be salad trays. Sandwich trays are at least 2s + 3.
Cost is least when sandwiches are exactly 2s + 3: 14(2s + 3) + 22s = 50s + 42 <= 600.
So s <= 11.16, and since s is a whole number, s = 11.
explanation.why: With 11 salad trays the cheapest valid order costs 50(11) + 42 = 592, within $600; 12 trays costs 642, over the budget.
explanation.pattern: Use the lower bound of the minimum requirement to get the cheapest case, then round down the whole-number answer.

items.stem: The solution set of the inequality \(kx - 5 < 3x + 9\) is all values of \(x\) such that \(x > -2\). What is the value of \(k\)?

steps: Collect x terms: (k - 3)x < 14.
The solution is x > -2, so dividing flipped the inequality; k - 3 must be negative, and 14/(k - 3) = -2.
So k - 3 = -7 and k = -4.
explanation.why: With k = -4: -4x - 5 < 3x + 9 gives -14 < 7x, so x > -2, as stated.
explanation.pattern: If the answer's direction differs from the natural one, the coefficient was negative; set the boundary equal and solve for the parameter.

items.stem:
If \(2 < a < 6\) and \(-3 < b < 1\), which of the following must be true?
I. \(a + b > -1\)
II. \(a - b < 6\)
III. \(b - a < -1\)

choices.slip: III is also true: b - a = -(a - b), and a - b is always greater than 1, so b - a is always less than -1.
choices.text: I only

choices.slip: a - b can be as large as nearly 9 (for example a = 5.9 and b = -2.9), so II is not always true.
choices.text: II only

choices.slip: II fails: a - b can reach nearly 9, which is above 6.
choices.text: I and II only
I and III only

steps: Add the bounds: 2 + (-3) < a + b < 6 + 1, so -1 < a + b < 7. Then a + b > -1: I is true.
For a - b, subtract the bounds the right way: 2 - 1 < a - b < 6 - (-3), so 1 < a - b < 9. a - b < 6 is not guaranteed: II is false.
Negating, b - a is between -9 and -1, so b - a < -1: III is true.
explanation.why: I and III hold across the whole range; II fails because a - b can be nearly 9.
explanation.pattern: To bound a difference, subtract the opposite end: the largest a - b uses the largest a and the smallest b.

items.stem: A baker sells muffins for $3.5 each. Each muffin costs $1.2 in ingredients, and the baker also pays a $90 permit fee for the day. What is the minimum number of muffins the baker must sell in a day to make a profit of at least $450?

steps: Only whole muffins can be sold, and 234 falls short, so round up to 235.
explanation.pattern: For a minimum with a whole-number count, round the boundary up; rounding down misses the goal.

items.stem: How many integer values of x satisfy \(-8 \le \frac{5 - 2x}{3} < 7\)?

steps: Multiply all parts by 3: -24 <= 5 - 2x < 21.
Subtract 5: -29 <= -2x < 16.
Divide by -2 and reverse both inequalities: -8 < x <= 14.5.
Integers from -7 to 14: 22.
explanation.why: x = -7 gives 19/3 < 7 and x = 14 gives -23/3 >= -8; x = -8 gives exactly 7 (not allowed) and x = 15 gives -25/3 < -8.
explanation.pattern: Dividing by a negative reverses both inequality signs, which also swaps which end is included. Count carefully including negatives.

items.stem: Real numbers a and b satisfy \(5 \le a + b \le 9\) and \(1 \le a - b \le 3\). What is the greatest possible value of \(3a + b\)?

steps: Write 3a + b as a combination of the two expressions: 3a + b = 2(a + b) + 1(a - b).
The greatest value is 2(9) + 1(3) = 21.
It can be reached: a + b = 9 and a - b = 3 give a = 6, b = 3, and 3(6) + 3 = 21.
explanation.why: Both upper bounds can hold at once, so the maximum of 2(a + b) + (a - b) is 18 + 3 = 21.
explanation.pattern: Rewrite the target as a sum of multiples of the constrained expressions (with positive multiples), then use the matching bounds, checking they are simultaneously reachable.

items.stem: In a course, the final grade is 35% of the midterm score plus 25% of the project score plus 40% of the final exam score. A student scored 78 on the midterm and 90 on the project. What is the minimum score on the final exam that gives the student a final grade of at least 85?

explanation.why: A final exam score of 88 gives 49.8 + 35.2 = 85 exactly.
explanation.pattern: A weighted grade is a sum of weight x score; the final exam only supplies its weighted share, so divide the shortfall by the weight (0.40), not by 1.

items.stem: The point \((p, 4)\) lies in the solution set of the system of inequalities \(y < 3x - 5\) and \(2x + y \le 23\). What is the sum of the least and greatest integer values of p?

steps: Substitute y = 4 into the first: 4 < 3p - 5, so 3p > 9 and p > 3.
Second: 2p + 4 <= 23, so p <= 9.5.
So 3 < p <= 9.5. Integers 4 through 9; least + greatest = 4 + 9 = 13.
explanation.why: p = 4 gives 4 < 7 and 12 <= 23; p = 9 gives 4 < 22 and 22 <= 23; p = 3 fails the strict first inequality and p = 10 fails the second.
explanation.pattern: Substituting a known coordinate turns the system into bounds on one variable; watch strict versus inclusive ends when picking integers.

items.stem: A cafe sold exactly 120 items one morning, and each item was either a muffin ($4) or a bagel ($3). Revenue was at least $410, and at least 40% of the items sold were bagels. How many different numbers of muffins could the cafe have sold?

steps: Let m be muffins; bagels = 120 - m. Revenue: 4m + 3(120 - m) = 360 + m >= 410, so m >= 50.
m can be any integer from 50 to 72: 72 - 50 + 1 = 23.
explanation.why: At m = 50 revenue is exactly 410 with 70 bagels; at m = 72 there are exactly 48 bagels and revenue is 432.
explanation.pattern: Two conditions give a lower and an upper bound; count the integers in the closed range (upper minus lower plus 1).

items.stem: What is the greatest integer \(x\) that satisfies \(\frac{5 - 3x}{4} \ge \frac{x - 2}{3} + 2\)?

steps: Multiply both sides by 12: \(3(5 - 3x) \ge 4(x - 2) + 24\), so \(15 - 9x \ge 4x + 16\).
Collect: \(-1 \ge 13x\), so \(x \le -\frac{1}{13}\). Dividing by the positive 13 does not flip the sign.
Since \(-\frac{1}{13}\) is a little below 0, the greatest integer is \(-1\), not 0.
explanation.why: x = -1 gives 2 >= 1 (true); x = 0 gives 1.25 >= 1.33 (false).
explanation.pattern: After solving, test the nearest integers: a bound just below zero rounds down to -1, not to 0.

items.stem: How many points \((x, y)\) with integer coordinates satisfy all three of the inequalities \(y \ge 2x - 3\), \(y \le -x + 9\), and \(x \ge 0\)?

steps: The first two bounds cross where \(2x - 3 = -x + 9\), so \(x = 4\). The region is nonempty only for \(0 \le x \le 4\).
For each integer \(x\), the number of \(y\) values is \((9 - x) - (2x - 3) + 1 = 13 - 3x\).
\(x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4\) give 13, 10, 7, 4, 1 points, and the total is 35.
explanation.why: 13 + 10 + 7 + 4 + 1 = 35; both boundary lines are included because the inequalities are not strict.
explanation.pattern: Count lattice points column by column: find the x-range from the intersection, then count the integers between the two bounds, endpoints included.

items.stem: A rectangular pen is to be built from 120 feet of fencing that encloses all four sides. The length must be at least 5 feet more than 2 times the width, and both dimensions must be whole numbers of feet. What is the greatest possible area of the pen, in square feet?

steps: Let the width be \(w\). The length is \(60 - w\) (half the perimeter minus \(w\)). The condition is \(60 - w \ge 2w + 5\), so \(w \le 18.33\), and with whole numbers \(w \le 18\).
The area \(w(60 - w)\) increases for \(w < 30\), so the greatest area under \(w \le 18\) is at \(w = 18\).
explanation.why: w = 19 would need length 41 >= 43, which fails; w = 18 gives 42 >= 41.
explanation.pattern: A constraint can stop you short of the unconstrained maximum (30 by 30): find the allowed range, then evaluate the area at the end nearest the peak.

items.stem: How many integers \(x\) satisfy both \(|3x - 5| < 16\) and \(2x + 1 \ge -4\)?

steps: From the absolute value: \(-16 < 3x - 5 < 16\), so \(-11 < 3x < 21\) and \(-3.67 < x < 7\).
From the second inequality: \(2x \ge -5\), so \(x \ge -2.5\).
Combine: \(-2.5 \le x < 7\). The integers are \(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\), which is 9.
explanation.why: x = -3 passes the first condition but fails the second (2(-3) + 1 = -5 < -4); x = 7 gives |16| which is not less than 16.
explanation.pattern: Solve each condition separately, intersect the intervals, and count integers, checking each endpoint for strict or inclusive.

items.stem: A florist has 500 stems. A small bouquet uses 4 stems and a large bouquet uses 9 stems. The number of small bouquets must be at least twice the number of large bouquets, and at least 10 large bouquets must be made. What is the greatest total number of bouquets the florist can make?

steps: Let s and L be the numbers of small and large bouquets: 4s + 9L <= 500, s >= 2L, L >= 10.
Each stem goes further on small bouquets, so total bouquets is maximized by making as few large ones as allowed: L = 10, so 4s <= 410 and s = 102 (which satisfies s >= 20).
Total = 102 + 10 = 112. For comparison, L = 11 gives s = 100 and a total of 111.
explanation.why: At L = 10, s = 102 uses 408 + 90 = 498 stems; any larger L lowers the total.
explanation.pattern: Maximizing a count under a cost cap means favoring the cheaper item; the minimum on the pricier item, not the ratio condition, is the binding constraint.

items.stem: In the xy-plane, a point \((x, y)\) satisfies \(y \geq 2x - 6\), \(y \leq -x + 9\), \(x \geq 0\), and \(y \geq 0\). What is the greatest possible value of \(3x + y\) for such a point?

steps: The region is a quadrilateral. Its corners: (0, 0), (3, 0) [where y = 2x - 6 meets y = 0], (5, 4) [where y = 2x - 6 meets y = -x + 9], and (0, 9).
Evaluate 3x + y at each corner: 0, 9, 19, 9.
The greatest value is 19, at (5, 4).
explanation.why: A linear expression on a bounded region reaches its maximum at a corner, and (5, 4) satisfies all four conditions.
explanation.pattern: Maximum of a linear expression over a region defined by inequalities occurs at a vertex; compute every vertex.

items.stem: The inequality \(ax + 7 \leq 2x - 5\), where \(a\) is a constant, has the solution set \(x \geq 3\). What is the value of \(a\)?

steps: Collect x terms: (a - 2)x <= -12.
Since the solution set is x >= 3 (the direction flipped), a - 2 must be negative, and dividing gives x >= -12/(a - 2).
explanation.why: Check: -2x + 7 <= 2x - 5 gives 12 <= 4x, so x >= 3.
explanation.pattern: If an inequality's direction reverses after dividing, the coefficient is negative; use that to fix the parameter.

items.stem: A student scored 78, 85, 91, and 66 on the first four of six quizzes. The student's grade is the mean of the five highest of the six quiz scores. The student scores the same whole number of points on each of the last two quizzes. What is the least score on each of those quizzes that gives a grade of at least 85?

steps: Try a score s that is at least 66: then 66 is dropped and the grade is (78 + 85 + 91 + 2s)/5 = (254 + 2s)/5.
Require (254 + 2s)/5 >= 85: 2s >= 171, so s >= 85.5, and the least whole number is 86.
A score below 66 would be the dropped one, giving (320 + s)/5 >= 85, which needs s >= 105 and is impossible.
explanation.why: At s = 86 the grade is 426/5 = 85.2; at s = 85 it is 424/5 = 84.8.
explanation.pattern: With a dropped score, check which score is dropped before writing the inequality, then consider the other case.

items.stem: A tank holds 8 inches of water at \(t = 0\) minutes. For the first 20 minutes the water level rises at a constant 1.5 inches per minute. After that, a drain opens and the level rises at a constant 0.6 inch per minute. The level is in the safe zone when it is at least 25 inches and at most 45 inches. For how many whole-number values of \(t\) with \(0 \leq t \leq 40\) is the level in the safe zone?

steps: For t <= 20 the level is 8 + 1.5t >= 25, so t >= 11.33 and t = 12, ..., 20. That is 9 values (the level at t = 20 is 38, under 45).
For t > 20 the level is 38 + 0.6(t - 20) <= 45, so t - 20 <= 11.67 and t = 21, ..., 31. That is 11 values.
explanation.why: At t = 31 the level is 44.6, and at t = 32 it is 45.2, just over the limit.
explanation.pattern: For piecewise rates, solve each piece's inequality on its own interval and count whole numbers in each.

items.stem: The sum of three consecutive multiples of 4 is greater than 100 and less than 130. What is the greatest possible value of the largest of the three numbers?

steps: Let the numbers be n, n + 4, n + 8 with n a multiple of 4. Their sum is 3n + 12.
100 < 3n + 12 < 130 gives 29.33... < n < 39.33..., so n is a multiple of 4 in that range: 32 or 36.
The greatest n is 36, so the largest of the three numbers is 36 + 8 = 44.
explanation.why: Check: 36 + 40 + 44 = 120, which is between 100 and 130; n = 40 would give 132, too big.
explanation.pattern: Write the sum in terms of the first term, solve the window, then keep only values allowed by the divisibility condition.

items.stem: A driver must travel 270 miles in at most 5 hours. She drives the first 120 miles at a constant 48 miles per hour. For the remainder of the trip she drives at a constant speed that is a whole number of miles per hour and does not exceed the speed limit of 65 miles per hour. How many different whole-number speeds for the remainder of the trip allow her to arrive on time?

steps: The first 120 miles take 120/48 = 2.5 hours, leaving at most 2.5 hours for the remaining 150 miles.
Her speed v must satisfy 150/v <= 2.5, so v >= 60.
The limit gives v <= 65, so the whole-number speeds are 60, 61, 62, 63, 64, 65: six values.
explanation.why: Exactly 60 mph takes exactly 2.5 hours, which still meets 'at most 5 hours', so both endpoints count.
explanation.pattern: Convert the time limit into a minimum speed (a reciprocal inequality), combine it with the maximum, and count the endpoints that are allowed.

items.stem: A customer applies a $25 coupon to the list price of an item, then a 20% discount is taken off the reduced amount, and then 8% sales tax is added to the discounted amount. The final total must be at most $500. What is the greatest whole-dollar list price the item can have?

steps: With list price p, the total is (p - 25)(0.80)(1.08) = 0.864(p - 25).
The greatest whole-dollar price is 603.
explanation.why: Check: p = 603 gives 0.864(578) = 499.39, within the limit; p = 604 gives 500.26, over the limit.
explanation.pattern: Apply the operations in the stated order and round the bound down, since the price must keep the total at or under the cap.

items.stem: For how many integer values of \(k\) does the point \((k, 2k)\) satisfy both \(y < 3x - 8\) and \(x + y \le 36\)?

steps: Substitute (k, 2k) into the first inequality: 2k < 3k - 8, so k > 8.
Substitute into the second: k + 2k <= 36, so k <= 12.
The integers with 8 < k <= 12 are 9, 10, 11, 12: four values.
explanation.why: The first inequality is strict (k = 8 gives 16 < 16, false) and the second includes its boundary (k = 12 gives 36 <= 36, true).
explanation.pattern: Substitute the parametric point into each inequality, solve for the parameter, and count integers carefully at strict and non-strict boundaries.

items.stem: A meal plan uses \(x\) servings of food A and \(y\) servings of food B, where \(x\) and \(y\) are nonnegative integers. Each serving of A has 30 grams of protein and 8 grams of fat. Each serving of B has 20 grams of protein and 3 grams of fat. The plan must provide at least 120 grams of protein and at most 30 grams of fat. What is the fewest total number of servings that meets both requirements?

steps: The conditions are 30x + 20y >= 120, i.e. 3x + 2y >= 12, and 8x + 3y <= 30.
Try 4 servings in total: x + y = 4 makes 3x + 2y = 8 + x, which needs x >= 4, so (4, 0); but its fat is 8(4) = 32 > 30. So 4 servings cannot work.
Try 5 servings: (2, 3) gives protein 60 + 60 = 120 and fat 16 + 9 = 25, which works. The minimum is 5.
explanation.why: With 4 servings the only protein-feasible mix is 4 servings of A, which breaks the fat limit; 5 servings works with (2, 3).
explanation.pattern: Combine the two constraints with the integer requirement: test the smallest totals in order and use one constraint to rule each out.

items.stem: Two angles of a triangle measure \(47^\circ\) and \(68^\circ\). What is the measure, in degrees, of the third angle?

steps: The angles of a triangle add to \(180^\circ\).
explanation.pattern: Triangle angle sum is 180°.

items.stem: Parallel lines \(p\) and \(q\) are intersected by transversal \(t\). One of the angles formed where \(t\) meets \(p\) measures \((3x + 10)^\circ\), and the corresponding angle where \(t\) meets \(q\) measures \((5x - 30)^\circ\). What is the value of \(x\)?

steps: When a transversal crosses parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal.
explanation.why: With x = 20 both angles are 70°.
explanation.pattern: Parallel lines: corresponding and alternate interior angles are equal; same-side interior angles add to 180°.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), the exterior angle at vertex \(C\) measures \(117^\circ\), and the measure of angle \(A\) is twice the measure of angle \(B\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(B\)?

steps: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two interior angles that are not next to it: \(A + B = 117\).
explanation.why: A = 78° and B = 39°, which add to 117°; angle C is then 63°, and 63 + 117 = 180 on the straight line.
explanation.pattern: Exterior angle = sum of the two remote interior angles. It saves finding the third angle.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), point \(D\) lies on \(\overline{AB}\) and point \(E\) lies on \(\overline{AC}\) such that \(\overline{DE}\) is parallel to \(\overline{BC}\). If \(AD = 6\), \(DB = 9\), and the area of triangle \(ADE\) is \(24\) square units, what is the area, in square units, of quadrilateral \(DBCE\)?

steps: \(\overline{DE} \parallel \overline{BC}\), so triangle \(ADE\) is similar to triangle \(ABC\) with ratio \(\frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{6}{6 + 9} = \frac{2}{5}\).
Areas scale by the square of the ratio: \(\frac{[ADE]}{[ABC]} = \frac{4}{25}\), so \([ABC] = 24 \cdot \frac{25}{4} = 150\).
The quadrilateral is what's left: \(150 - 24 = 126\).
explanation.why: The big triangle's sides are 5/2 times the small one's, so its area is 25/4 times 24, which is 150. Removing the small triangle leaves 126.
explanation.pattern: A parallel segment cuts off a similar triangle. Use the whole side (AD + DB) for the ratio, and square it for areas.

figure.alt: Triangle ABC with angle A marked 52 degrees, angle B marked 71 degrees, and angle C marked x degrees.

items.stem: In the triangle shown, what is the value of \(x\)?

steps: The angles of a triangle add to \(180^\circ\).
explanation.pattern: The three angles of any triangle sum to 180°.

figure.alt: Triangle ABC with point D on side AB and point E on side AC. Segment DE is drawn. AD is 6, DB is 3, DE is 8, and BC is x.

items.stem: In the figure, \(\overline{DE}\) is parallel to \(\overline{BC}\). What is the value of \(x\)?

choices.slip: Used DB/AD as the ratio: 8 × 3/6.
Added DB to DE instead of using a ratio.
Used AD/DB as the ratio: 8 × 6/3.

steps: Because \(\overline{DE} \parallel \overline{BC}\), triangle \(ADE\) is similar to triangle \(ABC\).
Matching sides: \(\frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{DE}{BC}\), where \(AB = 6 + 3 = 9\).
explanation.why: The small and large triangles are similar with ratio 6 : 9, so BC = 8 × 9/6 = 12.
explanation.pattern: A line parallel to one side of a triangle makes a smaller similar triangle. Use the whole side (AD + DB), not just DB.

figure.alt: Triangle ABC with side BC extended through C to point D. Angle ACD is marked 124 degrees and angle BAC is marked x degrees.

items.stem: In the figure, \(AB = AC\), and point \(C\) lies on \(\overline{BD}\). What is the value of \(x\)?

choices.slip: Stopped at the base angle.
Found the sum of the two base angles.
Took x to equal the outside angle.

steps: Angles \(ACB\) and \(ACD\) form a straight line: \(\angle ACB = 180 - 124 = 56^\circ\).
Since \(AB = AC\), the angles opposite those sides are equal: \(\angle ABC = 56^\circ\).
explanation.why: The base angles are each 56°, so the angle at A is 180 − 112 = 68.
explanation.pattern: In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite the equal sides are equal. Use a straight line (180°) to get an inside angle from an outside one.

figure.alt: Two horizontal lines, AB above CD. Point E is on AB and point F is on CD. Point P lies between the lines, to the right of E and F, joined to E and to F. Angle BEP is marked 38 degrees, angle DFP is marked 47 degrees, and angle EPF is marked x degrees.

items.stem: In the figure, \(\overline{AB}\) is parallel to \(\overline{CD}\), point \(E\) lies on \(\overline{AB}\), and point \(F\) lies on \(\overline{CD}\). What is the value of \(x\)?

choices.slip: Subtracted the two angles.
Found 180 − 85.
Found 180 − 47.

steps: Draw a line through \(P\) parallel to \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{CD}\). It splits angle \(EPF\) into two parts.
The upper part equals angle \(BEP\) (alternate interior angles): \(38^\circ\).
The lower part equals angle \(DFP\) (alternate interior angles): \(47^\circ\).
explanation.why: A parallel line through P splits the angle into 38° and 47°, so x = 85.
explanation.pattern: For a bend between two parallel lines, draw a third parallel line through the bend. The angle is the sum of the two marked angles.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), point \(D\) lies on \(\overline{AB}\) and point \(E\) lies on \(\overline{AC}\) so that \(\overline{DE}\) is parallel to \(\overline{BC}\). \(AD = 6\), \(DB = 4\), \(BC = 20\), and \(AC = 15\). What is the perimeter of quadrilateral \(DBCE\)?

steps: Since \(\overline{DE} \parallel \overline{BC}\), triangle \(ADE\) is similar to triangle \(ABC\) with ratio \(\frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{6}{10} = \frac{3}{5}\).
Perimeter of \(DBCE = DB + BC + CE + ED = 4 + 20 + 6 + 12 = 42\).
explanation.why: The similarity ratio is 3/5, so DE = 12 and EC = 6, and the perimeter is 4 + 20 + 6 + 12 = 42.
explanation.pattern: A line parallel to one side makes a similar small triangle. Use the ratio to find the missing sides, and use subtraction for the remaining pieces.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), \(AB = AC\). The bisector of \(\angle B\) and the bisector of \(\angle C\) intersect at point \(P\) inside the triangle, and \(\angle BPC = 124^\circ\). What is the measure, in degrees, of \(\angle A\)?

choices.slip: This is ∠PBC, half of a base angle.
This is a base angle, ∠B, not the vertex angle.
Halved ∠BPC without using the triangle.

steps: Let each base angle be \(2x\). The bisectors make \(\angle PBC = \angle PCB = x\).
In triangle \(PBC\): \(x + x + 124 = 180\), so \(x = 28\) and each base angle is \(56^\circ\).
explanation.why: Triangle PBC gives half a base angle of 28, so the base angles are 56 and the vertex angle is 68.
explanation.pattern: Angle bisectors split the base angles in half. Work in the small triangle first, then double back to the full triangle.

items.stem: A triangle has two sides of lengths \(7\) and \(12\), and its third side has an integer length \(x\). For how many values of \(x\) is the triangle obtuse?

steps: The triangle inequality gives \(5 < x < 19\), so \(x\) can be \(6, 7, \dots, 18\).
The angle opposite the longest side is obtuse when the square of that side exceeds the sum of the other two squares.
If 12 is longest: \(144 > 49 + x^2\), so \(x^2 < 95\), \(x \le 9\). That gives \(6, 7, 8, 9\): 4 values.
explanation.why: Five values of x (14 to 18) make x the obtuse side and four values (6 to 9) make 12 the obtuse side, so 9 in all.
explanation.pattern: Obtuse means longest side squared > sum of the other two squares. Check both cases for which side is longest.

items.stem: In triangle \(PQR\), \(PQ = PR\) and \(\angle QPR = 44^\circ\). Line \(\ell\) passes through \(P\) and is parallel to \(\overline{QR}\). Point \(S\) lies on \(\ell\) so that ray \(\overrightarrow{PS}\) points in the same direction as ray \(\overrightarrow{QR}\). What is the measure, in degrees, of \(\angle QPS\)?

choices.slip: This is the apex angle ∠QPR.
This is the base angle, which is the angle ∠QPS makes with the ray pointing the other way (toward Q's side).
Took the supplement of the apex angle (180 − 44).

steps: The base angles of the isosceles triangle are \(\frac{180 - 44}{2} = 68^\circ\).

The ray from \(P\) on the opposite side (pointing from \(R\) toward \(Q\)) makes a \(68^\circ\) angle with \(\overline{PQ}\), since it is parallel to \(\overline{QR}\) (alternate interior angles with \(\angle PQR\)).
\(\overrightarrow{PS}\) points the other way, so \(\angle QPS\) is the supplement: \(180 - 68 = 112\).
explanation.why: The base angle is 68, and the ray in the direction of QR forms the supplementary angle 180 - 68 = 112.
explanation.pattern: Alternate interior angles transfer a triangle's base angle to the parallel line. Then use a straight angle to get the angle on the other side.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), \(AB = AC = 10\) and \(BC = 12\). What is the length of the altitude from \(B\) to side \(\overline{AC}\)?

steps: Drop the altitude from \(A\) to \(\overline{BC}\). It bisects \(\overline{BC}\), so its length is \(\sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = 8\).
The same area equals \(\frac{1}{2}(AC)(h)\), where \(h\) is the altitude from \(B\): \(\frac{1}{2}(10)h = 48\), so \(h = 9.6\).
explanation.why: The area is 48 using base 12, and using base AC = 10 the matching height is 96/10 = 9.6.
explanation.pattern: When a triangle has two different altitudes, compute the area once and reuse it: area = 1/2 x any base x its altitude.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), the medians \(\overline{AD}\) and \(\overline{BE}\) intersect at point \(G\). \(AG = 3x + 2\) and \(GD = x + 4\). What is the length of \(\overline{AD}\)?

steps: The medians meet at the centroid, which divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1, so \(AG = 2 \cdot GD\).
explanation.why: The centroid sits two thirds of the way along a median, so AG = 2GD; solving gives x = 6, AG = 20, GD = 10, and AD = 30.
explanation.pattern: Medians meet at the centroid, 2/3 of the way from each vertex. Write AG = 2·GD, solve for x, then add the two parts.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), point \(D\) lies on \(\overline{AB}\) and point \(E\) lies on \(\overline{AC}\) such that \(\overline{DE}\) is parallel to \(\overline{BC}\). \(AD = 6\), \(DB = x\), \(DE = 8\), and \(BC = 14\). What is the value of \(x\)?

steps: Because \(\overline{DE} \parallel \overline{BC}\), triangle \(ADE\) is similar to triangle \(ABC\): \(\frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{DE}{BC}\).
explanation.why: The similar triangle compares AD to the whole side AB, not to DB; AB = 10.5, so DB = 4.5.
explanation.pattern: A segment parallel to a side cuts off a similar triangle. Match the small side to the whole side, then subtract to get the leftover piece.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), \(AB = 13\), \(AC = 15\), and \(BC = 14\). Point \(D\) lies on side \(\overline{BC}\) such that \(\overline{AD}\) is perpendicular to \(\overline{BC}\). What is the length of \(\overline{BD}\)?

steps: Let \(BD = y\), so \(DC = 14 - y\). The altitude \(AD\) satisfies \(13^2 - y^2 = 15^2 - (14 - y)^2\).
explanation.why: Both small right triangles share the altitude, so equating AD² from each gives BD = 5 (and DC = 9, AD = 12).
explanation.pattern: Drop an altitude and use the Pythagorean theorem in both right triangles; the shared altitude lets you set the two expressions for AD² equal.

items.stem: Three parallel lines \(\ell_1\), \(\ell_2\), and \(\ell_3\) are cut by two transversals, with \(\ell_2\) between \(\ell_1\) and \(\ell_3\). On the first transversal, the segment between \(\ell_1\) and \(\ell_2\) has length \(4\) and the segment between \(\ell_2\) and \(\ell_3\) has length \(6\). On the second transversal, these two segments have lengths \(x + 2\) and \(2x + 1\), respectively. What is the total length of the second transversal between \(\ell_1\) and \(\ell_3\)?

choices.slip: Gave the first transversal's total length, 4 + 6.
Gave only the longer segment.
Gave the value of x, not the length.

steps: Parallel lines cut transversals proportionally: \(\frac{x + 2}{2x + 1} = \frac{4}{6}\).
The segments are \(6\) and \(9\), so the total length is \(15\).
explanation.why: The segments on the second transversal must be in the ratio 4 : 6, which happens at x = 4, giving 6 and 9 and a total of 15.
explanation.pattern: Parallel lines make matching segments proportional. Solve for x, then answer with the quantity requested, not x.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), point \(D\) lies on \(\overline{BC}\) with \(BD : DC = 3 : 5\), and point \(E\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{AD}\). The area of triangle \(ABC\) is \(96\). What is the area of triangle \(CED\)?

steps: Triangles \(ABD\) and \(ADC\) share the altitude from \(A\), so their areas are in the ratio \(3 : 5\). Triangle \(ADC\) has area \(96 \cdot \frac{5}{8} = 60\).
Triangles \(CED\) and \(CEA\) share the altitude from \(C\) and have equal bases \(ED = EA\), so \(CED\) is half of \(ADC\).
Area of \(CED = \frac{60}{2} = 30\).
explanation.why: DC is 5/8 of the base, so triangle ADC is 60; E halves AD, so triangle CED is half of that: 30.
explanation.pattern: Triangles with a common altitude have areas proportional to their bases. Apply this twice: once to split by D, once to split by E.

items.stem: A regular polygon \(ABCDEFGHI\) has \(9\) sides, with its vertices labeled in order around the polygon. Diagonals \(AC\) and \(CE\) are drawn. What is the measure, in degrees, of \(\angle ACE\), the angle between these two diagonals at \(C\)?

choices.slip: Gave only the two removed base angles, 20 + 20.
Gave the supplement of the correct angle.
Gave the polygon's interior angle at C.

steps: Each interior angle of a regular 9-gon is \(\frac{7 \cdot 180}{9} = 140^\circ\).
Triangle \(ABC\) is isosceles with apex angle \(140^\circ\), so \(\angle BCA = \frac{180 - 140}{2} = 20^\circ\). Likewise \(\angle DCE = 20^\circ\).
Rays \(CA\) and \(CE\) lie inside the \(140^\circ\) angle at \(C\), each \(20^\circ\) from a side, so \(\angle ACE = 140 - 20 - 20 = 100^\circ\).
explanation.why: Diagonals CA and CE each cut 20 degrees off the 140-degree corner at C, leaving 100 degrees between them.
explanation.pattern: In a regular polygon, split interior angles with isosceles triangles; or use the inscribed angle: ∠ACE is half of the 200° arc AE that avoids C (5 of the 9 equal 40° arcs).

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), \(AB = 12\) and \(AC = 18\). Point \(D\) lies on side \(BC\) so that \(AD\) bisects angle \(BAC\). The area of triangle \(ABC\) is \(150\). What is the area of triangle \(ABD\)?

choices.slip: Assumed D is the midpoint of BC, so ABD is half the area.
Reversed the ratio, giving \(18/30\) of the area to ABD.
Used the ratio 12 : 18 as a fraction of the whole area instead of 12 : 30.

steps: By the angle bisector theorem, \(\frac{BD}{DC} = \frac{AB}{AC} = \frac{12}{18} = \frac{2}{3}\), so \(BD = \frac{2}{5}BC\).
Triangles \(ABD\) and \(ABC\) share the same height from \(A\), so their areas are in the ratio of their bases.
Area of \(ABD = \frac{2}{5} \cdot 150 = 60\).
explanation.why: BD is 2/5 of BC, and triangles with the same apex and bases on one line have areas in the same ratio.
explanation.pattern: Angle bisector theorem gives the base split; equal heights turn that split into an area split.

items.stem: Two vertical poles with heights \(15\) feet and \(10\) feet stand \(12\) feet apart on level ground. A wire is stretched from the top of each pole to the base of the other pole, and the two wires cross at a point. How many feet above the ground is the crossing point?

steps: Let the crossing point be a height \(y\) above the ground, with the foot of the vertical through it splitting the 12 feet into \(u\) (from the 15-foot pole) and \(12 - u\).
Similar triangles along each wire give \(\frac{y}{15} = \frac{12 - u}{12}\) and \(\frac{y}{10} = \frac{u}{12}\).
Adding: \(\frac{y}{15} + \frac{y}{10} = 1\), so \(y\left(\frac{1}{6}\right) = 1\) and \(y = 6\).
explanation.why: The distance between the poles drops out: 1/15 + 1/10 = 1/6 of the height equals 1, so y = 6.
explanation.pattern: Crossed-ladders result: 1/y = 1/h1 + 1/h2, independent of the distance between the poles.

items.stem: Triangle \(T_1\) has an area of \(240\) square units. Joining the midpoints of the sides of \(T_1\) forms triangle \(T_2\), and joining the midpoints of the sides of \(T_2\) forms triangle \(T_3\). What is the sum of the areas of \(T_2\) and \(T_3\)?

choices.slip: Found only the area of T2.
Halved the area at each step (120 + 60) instead of quartering.
Added the areas of T1 and T2 instead of T2 and T3.

steps: The midpoint triangle is similar to the original with ratio \(\frac{1}{2}\), so its area is \(\frac{1}{4}\) of the original.
explanation.why: Each midpoint triangle has 1/4 the area of the one before it: 60, then 15.
explanation.pattern: A midpoint triangle has half the side lengths, so one quarter of the area.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), angle \(A\) measures \(64^\circ\). The bisector of the exterior angle at \(B\) and the bisector of the exterior angle at \(C\) meet at point \(P\), outside the triangle. What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(BPC\)?

choices.slip: Gave half of angle A.
Gave 180 − 64, the supplement of angle A.
Used 90 + A/2, the angle formed by the interior bisectors at B and C.

steps: Angles \(B\) and \(C\) sum to \(180 - 64 = 116^\circ\).
The exterior angles at \(B\) and \(C\) are \(180 - B\) and \(180 - C\); half of each is \(90 - \frac{B}{2}\) and \(90 - \frac{C}{2}\), which are the base angles of triangle \(BPC\).
\(\angle BPC = 180 - \left(180 - \frac{B + C}{2}\right) = \frac{116}{2} = 58^\circ\) (equivalently, \(90 - \frac{64}{2}\)).
explanation.why: Triangle BPC has base angles 90 − B/2 and 90 − C/2, so its apex is (B + C)/2 = 58°.
explanation.pattern: Exterior-bisector angle = 90° − A/2; the interior-bisector angle is 90° + A/2.

items.stem: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is \(132^\circ\) greater than each exterior angle of the polygon. How many diagonals does the polygon have?

choices.slip: Stopped at the number of sides.
Counted all segments between vertices, n(n − 1)/2, including the sides.
Used n(n − 3) and forgot to divide by 2, since each diagonal was counted twice.

steps: Interior plus exterior angle is \(180^\circ\), and their difference is \(132^\circ\), so the exterior angle is \(\frac{180 - 132}{2} = 24^\circ\).
Exterior angles of a polygon sum to \(360^\circ\), so \(n = \frac{360}{24} = 15\).
The number of diagonals is \(\frac{n(n - 3)}{2} = \frac{15 \cdot 12}{2} = 90\).
explanation.why: The exterior angle is 24°, so the polygon has 15 sides and 15 · 12 ÷ 2 = 90 diagonals.
explanation.pattern: Interior + exterior = 180; n = 360 ÷ exterior; diagonals = n(n − 3)/2.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), \(AB = AC\). Point \(D\) lies on side \(BC\) so that \(AD = BD\) and \(AC = DC\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(BAC\)?

choices.slip: Found angle B but not angle BAC.
Gave angle ADC, the exterior angle of triangle ABD.
Gave the supplement of angle B.

steps: Let \(\angle B = x\). Since \(AB = AC\), \(\angle C = x\). Since \(AD = BD\), \(\angle BAD = x\).
\(\angle ADC\) is an exterior angle of triangle \(ABD\), so it equals \(x + x = 2x\). Since \(AC = DC\), the angles opposite those sides are equal: \(\angle DAC = \angle ADC = 2x\).
In triangle \(ABC\): \(x + x + (x + 2x) = 180\), so \(x = 36\), and \(\angle BAC = 3x = 108^\circ\).
explanation.why: Everything is expressed in x: B = C = x and A = 3x, so 5x = 180 and A = 108°.
explanation.pattern: Name one angle x, chase equal sides to angles, and use an exterior angle to link the two small triangles.

items.stem: In trapezoid \(ABCD\), side \(AB\) is parallel to side \(CD\), \(AB = 7x + (-1)\) and \(CD = 3x + 5\). The segment joining the midpoints of the two non-parallel sides has length \(22\) and crosses both diagonals. What is the length of the part of that segment that lies between the two diagonals?

steps: The midline equals the average of the bases: \(\frac{(7x - 1) + (3x + 5)}{2} = 22\), so \(10x + 4 = 44\) and \(x = 4\).
The bases are \(AB = 27\) and \(CD = 17\).
The midline meets each diagonal at the diagonal's midpoint, and the part between the diagonals has length \(\frac{27 - 17}{2} = 5\).
explanation.why: In triangles formed by the diagonals, the midline pieces on each side are half of AB and half of CD; the middle part is half the difference of the bases.
explanation.pattern: Midline of a trapezoid: whole = average of bases; the portion between the diagonals = half the difference.

items.stem: In parallelogram \(ABCD\), \(AB = 9\) and \(BC = 14\). The bisector of \(\angle A\) meets side \(BC\) at point \(E\), and the bisector of \(\angle D\) meets side \(BC\) at point \(F\). What is the length of \(EF\)?

choices.slip: Found only one bisector's effect (BC - AB) and ignored the second bisector.
Took EF equal to AB.
Added BE and CF (9 + 9) as if they did not overlap.

steps: Since \(AD \parallel BC\), \(\angle AEB = \angle EAD = \angle BAE\), so triangle \(ABE\) is isosceles and \(BE = AB = 9\).
In the same way \(CF = CD = AB = 9\), so \(BF = 14 - 9 = 5\).
\(E\) is 9 from \(B\) and \(F\) is 5 from \(B\), so \(EF = 9 - 5 = 4\).
explanation.why: Each bisector cuts off an isosceles triangle, and the two cut-off pieces BE and CF overlap by 2(9) - 14 = 4.
explanation.pattern: Angle bisectors in a parallelogram create isosceles triangles: BE = AB and CF = CD; measure from the same endpoint to compare positions.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), the bisectors of \(\angle B\) and \(\angle C\) meet at point \(I\) inside the triangle. \(\angle BIC = 124^\circ\) and \(\angle ABC = 64^\circ\). What is the measure, in degrees, of \(\angle ACB\)?

choices.slip: Found half of angle C (56 - 32) and did not double it.
Gave 180 - 124, the sum of the two half-angles at B and C.
Gave the measure of angle A.

steps: In triangle \(BIC\): \(\angle IBC + \angle ICB = 180 - 124 = 56\).
These are half of \(\angle B\) and half of \(\angle C\), so \(\angle B + \angle C = 112\).
explanation.why: The two half-angles sum to 56, so B + C = 112.
explanation.pattern: Angle bisectors halve their angles: use the triangle containing the incenter, then double.

items.stem: Triangle \(ABC\) is similar to triangle \(DEF\), with side \(BC\) corresponding to side \(EF\). The ratio \(BC : EF\) is \(4 : 5\), and \(BC = 16\). The area of triangle \(DEF\) is \(45\) square units greater than the area of triangle \(ABC\). What is the length of the altitude of triangle \(DEF\) to side \(EF\)?

choices.slip: Found the altitude of triangle ABC to BC, not of DEF.
Used the area of DEF with the side BC = 16 instead of EF = 20.
Used the ratio of sides 4:5 as the ratio of areas, giving DEF an area of 225.

steps: Areas of similar figures are in the ratio of the squares: \(16 : 25\). The difference of 9 parts is 45, so one part is 5.
Area of \(DEF = 25 \times 5 = 125\), and \(EF = 16 \times \frac{5}{4} = 20\).
explanation.why: Area of DEF is 125 and its side EF is 20, so its altitude is 250/20.
explanation.pattern: Similar figures: lengths scale by k, areas by k^2; use the area difference to find the actual areas, then work with the correct corresponding side.

items.stem: Each interior angle of a regular polygon measures \(60^\circ\) more than \(2\) times the measure of an exterior angle of the polygon. How many diagonals does the polygon have?

choices.slip: Stopped after finding the number of sides.
Counted all segments joining pairs of vertices (9 choose 2), sides included.
Used n(n - 3) and forgot to divide by 2 for double counting.

steps: Interior \(+\) exterior \(= 180^\circ\), so \(180 - e = 2e + 60\), giving \(e = 40^\circ\).
Exterior angles sum to \(360^\circ\): \(n = 360/40 = 9\).
Diagonals \(= \frac{n(n - 3)}{2} = \frac{9 \cdot 6}{2} = 27\).
explanation.why: Exterior angle 40 degrees gives 9 sides; 9 sides give 27 diagonals.
explanation.pattern: Regular polygon: interior + exterior = 180, exterior angles sum to 360, then count diagonals with n(n-3)/2.

items.stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, point \(P\) lies on the \(x\)-axis and is the same distance from \(A(1, 2)\) as from \(B(7, 10)\). What is the area of triangle \(PAB\)?

steps: Triangle \(PAB\) is isosceles; the altitude from \(P\) to \(AB\) has length \(\sqrt{125 - 5^2} = 10\), so the area is \(\frac{1}{2}(10)(10) = 50\).
explanation.why: P lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB; its distance from AB is 10.
explanation.pattern: Equidistant points satisfy a linear equation; then use the isosceles triangle's altitude (or the shoelace formula) for area.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), point \(G\) is the centroid. A line through \(G\) parallel to \(\overline{BC}\) meets \(\overline{AB}\) at \(D\) and \(\overline{AC}\) at \(E\). The area of trapezoid \(DBCE\) is \(100\). What is the area of triangle \(ABC\)?

steps: The centroid lies \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the way along the median from \(A\) to the midpoint of \(\overline{BC}\), so the line through \(G\) is \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the way from \(A\) to \(\overline{BC}\).
Triangle \(ADE\) is similar to triangle \(ABC\) with ratio \(\frac{2}{3}\), so its area is \(\frac{4}{9}\) of the whole.
The trapezoid is the remaining \(\frac{5}{9}\): \(\frac{5}{9}\,[ABC] = 100\), so \([ABC] = 180\).
explanation.why: The cut-off triangle has area 4/9 of the whole, so the trapezoid is 5/9, not 1/3.
explanation.pattern: Centroid plus parallel line: use the 2:1 median ratio as a similarity ratio, then square it for area.

items.stem: An isosceles triangle has a perimeter of \(50\) and an altitude of \(15\) drawn to its base. What is the area of the triangle?

steps: Let each equal side be \(L\), so the base is \(50 - 2L\) and the altitude splits it into halves of \(25 - L\).
By the Pythagorean theorem, \(15^2 + (25 - L)^2 = L^2\), so \(225 + 625 - 50L = 0\) and \(L = 17\).
The base is \(50 - 34 = 16\), and the area is \(\frac{1}{2}(16)(15) = 120\).
explanation.why: The perimeter fixes the half-base as 25 minus a leg, which the altitude's right triangle then determines.
explanation.pattern: Isosceles with perimeter and altitude: write the half-base in terms of the leg and apply the Pythagorean theorem.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle B = 84^\circ\) and \(\angle C = 36^\circ\). The altitude from \(A\) and the bisector of \(\angle A\) both meet \(\overline{BC}\). What is the measure, in degrees, of the angle between the altitude and the bisector?

steps: \(\angle A = 180^\circ - 84^\circ - 36^\circ = 60^\circ\), so the bisector makes a \(30^\circ\) angle with \(\overline{AB}\).
In the right triangle formed by the altitude and side \(AB\), the altitude makes an angle of \(90^\circ - 84^\circ = 6^\circ\) with \(\overline{AB}\).
Both lines lie on the same side of \(\overline{AB}\) inside the triangle, so the angle between them is \(30^\circ - 6^\circ = 24^\circ\) (which equals \(\frac{1}{2}|84 - 36|\)).
explanation.why: Measure both lines from the same side, AB, and subtract: 30 minus 6.
explanation.pattern: Altitude and bisector from one vertex: the angle between them is half the difference of the base angles.

items.stem: An equilateral triangle has a perimeter of \(36\sqrt{3}\). A point inside the triangle is \(5\) units from one side and \(7\) units from a second side. How far is the point from the third side?

choices.slip: Used the side length \(12\sqrt{3}\) in place of the altitude.
Gave half the side length.
Subtracted only the first distance from the altitude \(18\).

steps: The side is \(36\sqrt{3}/3 = 12\sqrt{3}\), so the altitude is \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}(12\sqrt{3}) = 18\).

For any interior point of an equilateral triangle, the three distances to the sides add up to the altitude (splitting the triangle into three triangles of equal base: \(\frac{1}{2}s(d_1 + d_2 + d_3) = \frac{1}{2}sh\)).
The third distance is \(18 - 5 - 7 = 6\).
explanation.why: Splitting the triangle into three by joining the point to the vertices shows the distances sum to the altitude.
explanation.pattern: Equilateral triangle: sum of perpendicular distances from an interior point equals the altitude.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), \(AB = 18\) and \(AC = 30\). The bisector of \(\angle A\) meets \(\overline{BC}\) at \(D\), where \(BD = 2x + 1\) and \(DC = 4x - 3\). What is the perimeter of triangle \(ABC\)?

steps: By the angle bisector theorem, \(\frac{BD}{DC} = \frac{AB}{AC} = \frac{18}{30}\), so \(30(2x + 1) = 18(4x - 3)\).
Perimeter \(= 18 + 30 + 40 = 88\). (Check: \(18 + 30 = 48 > 40\), so the triangle exists.)
explanation.why: Set the segment ratio equal to the side ratio, solve for x, and add the whole side BC to the two given sides.
explanation.pattern: Angle bisector theorem with algebra: cross-multiply, solve, then build the requested total.

items.stem: In a right triangle, the median drawn to the hypotenuse has length \(13\), and one leg has length \(10\). What is the perimeter of the triangle?

choices.slip: Treated the median as the hypotenuse, so the other leg was \(\sqrt{169 - 100}\).
Left out the second leg: \(10 + 26 = 36\).
Found the other leg \(24\) correctly but used the median \(13\) in place of the hypotenuse.

steps: In a right triangle the median to the hypotenuse equals half the hypotenuse, so the hypotenuse is \(2 \cdot 13 = 26\).
The other leg is \(\sqrt{26^2 - 10^2} = \sqrt{576} = 24\).
explanation.why: The median to the hypotenuse is the circumradius, half the hypotenuse.
explanation.pattern: Right triangle median: the median to the hypotenuse is half the hypotenuse.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), point \(D\) lies on side \(BC\) so that \(BD = AD\) and \(AC = DC\). If the measure of angle \(ACB\) is 84 degrees, what is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(BAC\)?

steps: Let \(\angle B = x\). Since \(BD = AD\), \(\angle BAD = x\), so the exterior angle \(\angle ADC = 2x\).
Since \(AC = DC\), \(\angle DAC = \angle ADC = 2x\). In triangle \(ADC\), \(2x + 2x + 84 = 180\), so \(x = 24\).
\(\angle BAC = \angle BAD + \angle DAC = x + 2x = 72\).
explanation.why: Check: angles of ABC are 24, 72, 84, which sum to 180.
explanation.pattern: Chain two isosceles triangles with the exterior angle theorem; express everything in one base angle.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), \(M\) is the midpoint of side \(BC\) and \(G\) is the centroid. The area of triangle \(ABC\) is 90. Point \(E\) is the midpoint of segment \(AG\). What is the area of triangle \(EBG\)?

choices.slip: Took EG as one-sixth of AM, halving twice.
Used one-ninth of the whole triangle, treating the sub-triangle as a scale copy.
Found the area of triangle ABG (one-third of the whole), not EBG.

steps: Triangle \(ABM\) has half the area of \(ABC\), so its area is 45.
\(G\) lies two-thirds of the way from \(A\) to \(M\), so \(AG = \frac{2}{3}AM\), and \(E\) is the midpoint of \(AG\), so \(EG = \frac{1}{3}AM\).
Triangles \(EBG\) and \(ABM\) have the same height from \(B\) to line \(AM\), so \([EBG] = \frac{EG}{AM} \cdot 45 = 15\).
explanation.why: Triangles sharing a vertex and with bases on the same line have areas in the ratio of the bases; here the base ratio is 1/3 of half the triangle.
explanation.pattern: Area ratios from a common altitude: reduce to bases on one line, then multiply the fractions.

items.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), \(AB = 13\), \(AC = 15\), and \(BC = 14\). A line through the incenter of the triangle, parallel to \(BC\), meets \(AB\) at \(D\) and \(AC\) at \(E\). What is the length of \(DE\)?

steps: Because \(DE \parallel BC\), \(\angle DIB = \angle IBC = \angle DBI\), so \(DB = DI\). Likewise \(EC = EI\). Hence \(DE = BD + CE\).
The perimeter of triangle \(ADE\) is \(AD + DE + EA = AD + BD + CE + EA = AB + AC = 28\).
Triangle \(ADE\) is similar to \(ABC\) (perimeter 42), so \(DE = 14 \cdot \frac{28}{42} = \frac{28}{3}\).
explanation.why: The two isosceles triangles from the angle bisectors make the perimeter of ADE equal to AB + AC, which fixes the similarity ratio at 28/42.
explanation.pattern: A line through the incenter parallel to a side: the bisector angles create isosceles triangles, so the cut-off segment equals the sum of the two side pieces.

items.stem: \((x + 6)(2x - 9) = 0\). What is the positive solution to the given equation?

steps: A product is 0 only when a factor is 0: \(x + 6 = 0\) or \(2x - 9 = 0\).
The first gives \(x = -6\), which is negative.
The second gives \(x = \frac{9}{2}\), or 4.5.
explanation.why: Setting 2x − 9 = 0 gives x = 9/2, the only positive solution.
explanation.pattern: Zero-product property: set each factor equal to 0 separately.

items.stem: \(\sqrt{x + 5} = 4\). What value of \(x\) satisfies the given equation?

steps: Square both sides: \(x + 5 = 16\).
explanation.why: √16 = 4, so x + 5 must be 16, and x = 11.
explanation.pattern: Undo a square root by squaring both sides, then check the answer in the original equation.

items.stem: If \(2^{x+1} = 32\), what is the value of \(x\)?

choices.slip: Found the exponent x + 1 = 5 but forgot to subtract 1.
Divided 32 by 2 and subtracted 1, treating the exponent as a multiplier.
Divided 32 by the base 2 instead of using exponents.

steps: Write \(32\) as a power of 2: \(32 = 2^5\).
Equal bases mean equal exponents: \(x + 1 = 5\).
explanation.pattern: Rewrite both sides with the same base, then set the exponents equal.

items.stem: What is the sum of the solutions to the equation \(2x(x - 3) = x + 15\)?

steps: Expand and move everything to one side: \(2x^2 - 6x - x - 15 = 0\), so \(2x^2 - 7x - 15 = 0\).
explanation.why: The solutions are −1.5 and 5, which add to 3.5. (For ax² + bx + c = 0 the sum is −b/a = 7/2.)
explanation.pattern: Collect everything on one side before factoring; the sum of the solutions of ax² + bx + c = 0 is −b/a.

items.stem:
\(y = x^2 - 4x + 7\)
\(y = 2x - 1\)
The graphs of the given equations in the \(xy\)-plane intersect at the points \((x_1, y_1)\) and \((x_2, y_2)\). What is the value of \(y_1 + y_2\)?

steps: Set the right sides equal: \(x^2 - 4x + 7 = 2x - 1\), so \(x^2 - 6x + 8 = 0\).
explanation.why: The intersection points are (2, 3) and (4, 7), whose y-values add to 10.
explanation.pattern: Substitute to get one equation in x, solve, then plug back into the simpler (linear) equation for y.

items.stem: Which of the following gives all the solutions to the equation \(\sqrt{2x + 7} = x - 4\)?

choices.slip: Kept the extraneous solution and dropped the real one.
Did not check the answers; x = 1 makes the right side −3, but a square root cannot be negative.
x = 9 checks out, so there is a solution.
choices.text: There is no solution.

steps: Square both sides: \(2x + 7 = x^2 - 8x + 16\), so \(x^2 - 10x + 9 = 0\).
Check \(x = 1\): \(\sqrt{9} = 3\) but \(1 - 4 = -3\). It fails.
Check \(x = 9\): \(\sqrt{25} = 5\) and \(9 - 4 = 5\). It works.
explanation.why: Squaring can create a false solution; only x = 9 makes both sides equal, because a square root is never negative.
explanation.pattern: After squaring both sides, always check each answer in the original equation.

items.stem: If \(5x^2 - 30x = -35\), what is the value of \(x^2 - 6x + 4\)?

steps: Divide both sides by \(5\): \(x^2 - 6x = -7\).
explanation.why: The target expression is the given one divided by 5, plus 4, so no need to find x at all.
explanation.pattern: When asked for an expression, look for a way to scale the given equation into it before solving for x.

items.stem:
\(y = x^2 + 6x + c\)
\(y = -2x + 3\)
In the given system of equations, \(c\) is a constant. The system has exactly one solution. What is the value of \(c\)?

steps: Set the right sides equal: \(x^2 + 6x + c = -2x + 3\), so \(x^2 + 8x + (c - 3) = 0\).
Exactly one solution means the discriminant is 0: \(8^2 - 4(1)(c - 3) = 0\).
explanation.why: With c = 19 the equation becomes x² + 8x + 16 = (x + 4)² = 0, a single solution x = −4: the line touches the parabola once.
explanation.pattern: One intersection of a line and a parabola means the combined quadratic has discriminant b² − 4ac = 0.

items.stem: In the equation \(|2x - k| = 10\), \(k\) is a positive constant. The product of the solutions to the equation is \(24\). What is the value of \(k\)?

explanation.why: With k = 14 the solutions are 12 and 2, and 12 × 2 = 24.
explanation.pattern: Write both cases of an absolute value equation in terms of the constant, then apply the condition to them.

items.stem:
\(\frac{2x}{x - 3} + 1 = \frac{k}{x - 3}\)
In the given equation, \(k\) is a constant. For what value of \(k\) does the equation have no solution?

steps: Multiply both sides by \(x - 3\) (allowed only when \(x \ne 3\)): \(2x + (x - 3) = k\), so \(3x - 3 = k\).
This gives exactly one candidate, \(x = \frac{k + 3}{3}\).
The equation has no solution only when that candidate is not allowed, that is when \(\frac{k + 3}{3} = 3\).
explanation.why: With k = 6 the only candidate is x = 3, which makes the denominators 0, so it is thrown out and nothing is left.
explanation.pattern: Clearing denominators can create a solution that is not allowed. A rational equation has no solution when its only candidate is an excluded value.

items.stem:
\(|x^2 - 6x + 5| = k\)
For how many integer values of \(k\) does the given equation have exactly four distinct real solutions?

steps: The equation means \(x^2 - 6x + 5 = k\) or \(x^2 - 6x + 5 = -k\). Let \(f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 5 = (x - 3)^2 - 4\), with minimum value \(-4\).
For \(k > 0\), \(f(x) = k\) always has two solutions (k is above the minimum).
\(f(x) = -k\) has two solutions when \(-k > -4\), one when \(k = 4\), none when \(k > 4\).
So four solutions happen when \(0 < k < 4\): \(k = 1, 2, 3\). That is 3 values.
explanation.why: k = 4 gives only three solutions and k = 0 gives only two, so exactly 1, 2 and 3 work.
explanation.pattern: For |f(x)| = k, split into f = k and f = -k and count solutions of each using the vertex.

items.stem:
\((x - 3)^2 + y^2 = 8\)
\(y = x + k\)
In the given system of equations, \(k\) is a constant. The system has exactly one solution. What is the sum of all possible values of \(k\)?

steps: Substitute \(y = x + k\): \((x - 3)^2 + (x + k)^2 = 8\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 + (2k - 6)x + k^2 + 1 = 0\).
One solution means discriminant 0: \((2k - 6)^2 - 8(k^2 + 1) = -4k^2 - 24k + 28 = 0\), so \(k^2 + 6k - 7 = 0\).
\((k + 7)(k - 1) = 0\), so \(k = -7\) or \(k = 1\). Their sum is \(-6\) (also given by -b/a).
explanation.why: The line is tangent to the circle for k = 1 and k = -7, which add to -6.
explanation.pattern: A line meets a circle exactly once when it is tangent; substitute and set the discriminant to 0, then use the sum of the roots.

items.stem:
\(3x^4 - 20x^2 - 32 = 0\)
What is the sum of the squares of all real solutions to the given equation?

steps: So \(u = -\frac{4}{3}\) or \(u = 8\). Since \(u = x^2 \ge 0\), reject \(-\frac{4}{3}\).
The real solutions are \(x = \pm 2\sqrt{2}\); the sum of their squares is \(8 + 8 = 16\).
explanation.why: Only u = 8 gives real x, so the two real solutions each square to 8 and the sum is 16.
explanation.pattern: In a quadratic-in-x² equation, discard negative values of x²; each valid value gives two real x.

items.stem:
\(y = x^2 - 4x + 1\)
\(y = x + 5\)
The solutions to the given system of equations are \((x_1, y_1)\) and \((x_2, y_2)\). What is the value of \(y_1 + y_2\)?

steps: Set the expressions equal: \(x^2 - 4x + 1 = x + 5\), so \(x^2 - 5x - 4 = 0\). The discriminant is 41, so the solutions are irrational and there is no need to find them.
By the sum of the roots, \(x_1 + x_2 = 5\).
Since \(y = x + 5\) for both points, \(y_1 + y_2 = (x_1 + x_2) + 10 = 15\).
explanation.why: y1 + y2 = (x1 + x2) + 2(5) = 5 + 10 = 15, and x1 + x2 = 5 comes from the sum of the roots.
explanation.pattern: Use the sum of the roots of the combined quadratic and the linear equation to add the y-values without solving.

items.stem:
\(9^x - 4 \cdot 3^{x + 1} + 27 = 0\)
What is the sum of all solutions to the given equation?

steps: \(3^x = 3\) gives \(x = 1\); \(3^x = 9\) gives \(x = 2\). The sum is 3.
explanation.why: The solutions are x = 1 and x = 2.
explanation.pattern: Turn an exponential equation into a quadratic with u = base^x, and remember 3^(x+1) = 3 · 3^x.

items.stem:
\(\frac{x^2 - 16}{x - 4} = 3x + k\)
The constant \(k\) makes the given equation have no solution for exactly one value. What is that value of \(k\)?

steps: For \(x \ne 4\), \(\frac{x^2 - 16}{x - 4} = x + 4\). So the equation becomes \(x + 4 = 3x + k\), giving \(x = \frac{4 - k}{2}\).
This is the only candidate. It is invalid when it equals the excluded value 4: \(\frac{4 - k}{2} = 4\), so \(k = -4\).
For every other k the candidate is a different number and works, so the equation has no solution only for \(k = -4\).
explanation.why: At k = -4, the only candidate is x = 4, which is excluded because it makes the denominator 0.
explanation.pattern: After cancelling a factor, the original equation still excludes the cancelled value; no solution occurs when the only candidate is that value.

items.stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, the line \(y = x + 2\) intersects the circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 50\) at two points. What is the square of the distance between these two points?

steps: Both points lie on a line of slope 1, so \(y_1 - y_2 = x_1 - x_2\) and the squared distance is \(96 + 96 = 192\).
explanation.why: The x-coordinates differ by a squared amount of 96, and so do the y-coordinates, so the squared distance is 192.
explanation.pattern: Use the sum and product of the roots to get the squared difference without finding the irrational roots.

items.stem: Working together, two pumps fill a tank in 2 hours. Working alone, the slower pump takes 3 hours longer than the faster pump to fill the tank. How many hours does the slower pump take to fill the tank alone?

steps: Let the faster pump take \(t\) hours alone. Rates add: \(\frac{1}{t} + \frac{1}{t + 3} = \frac{1}{2}\).
Only \(t = 3\) is possible, so the faster pump takes 3 hours and the slower pump takes \(3 + 3 = 6\) hours.
explanation.why: The faster pump takes 3 hours alone, so the slower pump takes 6; check: 1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2.
explanation.pattern: Add rates (1/time) for jobs done together, solve the rational equation, reject the negative time, then answer for the requested pump.

items.stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, the graphs of \(y = x^2 - 6x + 14\) and \(y = -2x + k\), where \(k\) is a constant, intersect at exactly two points. Which of the following describes all possible values of \(k\)?

choices.slip: Included k = 10, where the line is tangent and meets the parabola at only one point.
Reversed the inequality: a negative discriminant means no intersection.
Dropped the factor of 4 from the discriminant (used 16 - (14 - k) > 0).

steps: Set the expressions equal: \(x^2 - 6x + 14 = -2x + k\), so \(x^2 - 4x + (14 - k) = 0\).
Two intersection points require two distinct real solutions: discriminant \(16 - 4(14 - k) > 0\).
\(4k - 40 > 0\), so \(k > 10\). At \(k = 10\) the line is tangent, giving only one point.
explanation.why: A positive discriminant 4k - 40 requires k > 10; k = 10 gives a single tangent point.
explanation.pattern: Set the two expressions equal, move everything to one side, and require the discriminant to be strictly positive for exactly two intersections.

items.stem: What is the solution to the equation \(\sqrt{x + 11} - \sqrt{x - 1} = 2\)?

steps: Isolate one radical: \(\sqrt{x + 11} = 2 + \sqrt{x - 1}\).
Square both sides: \(x + 11 = 4 + 4\sqrt{x - 1} + x - 1\), so \(8 = 4\sqrt{x - 1}\).
explanation.why: After squaring, the x terms cancel and leave sqrt(x - 1) = 2, so x = 5, which checks.
explanation.pattern: With two radicals, isolate one, square, then isolate the remaining radical and square again; always check in the original equation.

items.stem: What is the sum of all real solutions to the equation \((x - 3)^{2/3} = 25\)?

steps: The exponent \(\frac{2}{3}\) means squaring a cube root, so \(x - 3\) can be positive or negative: \((x - 3)^2 = 25^3 = 15625\).
explanation.why: Both x - 3 = 125 and x - 3 = -125 satisfy the equation, so the solutions 128 and -122 sum to 6.
explanation.pattern: An even numerator in a rational exponent makes the base able to be negative as well as positive, giving two real solutions.

items.stem: If \(x^2 - y^2 = 40\) and \(x + y = 8\), what is the value of \(xy\)?

steps: Add and subtract: \(x + y = 8\) and \(x - y = 5\) give \(2x = 13\), \(x = 6.5\), and \(y = 1.5\).
explanation.why: x - y = 5 and x + y = 8 give x = 6.5 and y = 1.5, so xy = 9.75.
explanation.pattern: Factor a difference of squares to turn a nonlinear equation into a linear system.

items.stem: What is the sum of all solutions to the equation \(x - 7\sqrt{x} + 10 = 0\)?

steps: So \(\sqrt{x} = 2\) or \(\sqrt{x} = 5\), giving \(x = 4\) or \(x = 25\). Both satisfy the original equation since \(\sqrt{x}\) is positive.
The sum is \(4 + 25 = 29\).
explanation.why: Substituting u = sqrt(x) gives u = 2 or 5, so x = 4 or 25, and the sum is 29 (not 7, the sum of the u-values).
explanation.pattern: Spot a quadratic in disguise with a substitution, then convert the solutions back to the original variable before summing.

items.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 34 centimeters and a diagonal of length 13 centimeters. What is the area, in square centimeters, of the rectangle?

steps: Let the sides be \(\ell\) and \(w\). Then \(\ell + w = 17\) and \(\ell^2 + w^2 = 169\).
Check: the sides are 12 and 5, and \(12^2 + 5^2 = 169\).
explanation.why: Squaring the semi-perimeter and subtracting the diagonal squared leaves twice the area: 2lw = 120, so the area is 60.
explanation.pattern: Use (l + w)^2 = l^2 + w^2 + 2lw to connect perimeter and diagonal to area without solving for each side.

items.stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, the parabola \(y = x^2 - 2x\) and the line \(y = 2x + 5\) intersect at points \(P\) and \(Q\). What is the value of \(PQ^2\)?

steps: The points are \(P(-1, 3)\) and \(Q(5, 15)\).
explanation.why: The intersections are (-1, 3) and (5, 15), giving 36 + 144 = 180.
explanation.pattern: Substitute to find both x-values, use the line to get y-values, and apply the distance formula; leave the answer squared.

items.stem: For real numbers \(x\) and \(y\), \(x - y = 3\) and \(x^2 + y^2 = 29\). What is the value of \(x^3 - y^3\)?

explanation.why: xy = 10 from the squared difference, and the factored difference of cubes gives 3 * 39 = 117 for both solution pairs.
explanation.pattern: Use the identity (x - y)^2 to get xy, then factor x^3 - y^3 instead of solving for x and y.

items.stem: What is the sum of all real solutions to the equation \(8^{x + 1} \cdot 2^{x} = 4^{x^2 - 1}\)?

steps: Write every base as a power of 2: \(2^{3(x + 1)} \cdot 2^x = 2^{2(x^2 - 1)}\).
Equate exponents: \(3x + 3 + x = 2x^2 - 2\), so \(2x^2 - 4x - 5 = 0\).
The discriminant is \(16 + 40 > 0\), so there are two real solutions with sum \(\frac{4}{2} = 2\).
explanation.why: The exponent equation 2x^2 - 4x - 5 = 0 has two real roots whose sum is 2.
explanation.pattern: Rewrite with a common base, equate exponents, then use the sum of roots after confirming the discriminant is positive.

items.stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, two different lines pass through the point \((2, -3)\) and are each tangent to the parabola \(y = x^2 + 1\). What is the product of the slopes of these two lines?

steps: A line through \((2, -3)\) with slope \(m\) is \(y = m(x - 2) - 3\). Setting it equal to \(y = x^2 + 1\) gives \(x^2 - mx + 2m + 4 = 0\).
Tangency means the discriminant is zero: \(m^2 - 4(2m + 4) = m^2 - 8m - 16 = 0\).
The two slopes are the roots of this equation, so their product is \(-16\).
explanation.why: The discriminant condition is a quadratic in m, and the product of its roots is -16.
explanation.pattern: Make the intersection equation quadratic in x, set its discriminant to zero, and treat the result as a quadratic in the slope; use Vieta for the product.

items.stem: A boat can travel at a constant speed of 10 kilometers per hour in still water. The boat travels 24 kilometers upstream on a river with a constant current of \(c\) kilometers per hour, then returns the same 24 kilometers downstream. The upstream trip takes exactly 1 hour longer than the downstream trip. What is the value of \(c\)?

steps: Upstream speed is \(10 - c\) and downstream speed is \(10 + c\). Time equation: \(\frac{24}{10 - c} - \frac{24}{10 + c} = 1\).
\(c^2 + 48c - 100 = 0\) factors as \((c + 50)(c - 2) = 0\). Since the current is positive, \(c = 2\).
explanation.why: The quadratic c^2 + 48c - 100 = 0 has the positive solution 2, and 24/8 - 24/12 = 1 checks.
explanation.pattern: Write time = distance / rate for both directions, clear denominators, and reject the negative root.

items.stem: The circle in the \(xy\)-plane is given by \(x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 10y = c\), where \(c\) is a constant. The circle is tangent to the line \(y = x + 2\). What is the value of \(c\)?

steps: Substitute \(y = x + 2\): \(x^2 + (x + 2)^2 - 6x + 10(x + 2) - c = 0\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 + 8x + 24 - c = 0\).
Tangency means exactly one intersection, so the discriminant is zero: \(64 - 8(24 - c) = 0\).
explanation.why: Substituting the line gives a quadratic whose discriminant is 64 - 8(24 - c); setting it to 0 gives c = 16.
explanation.pattern: A line is tangent to a circle exactly when substituting it gives a quadratic with discriminant 0.

items.stem: For how many integer values of \(k\) with \(-10 \le k \le 10\) does the equation \(\sqrt{x + k} = x - 2\) have exactly one real solution?

steps: Squaring: \(x + k = (x-2)^2\), so \(x^2 - 5x + 4 - k = 0\), with discriminant \(9 + 4k\). Valid solutions need \(x \ge 2\).
The roots are \(x = (5 \pm \sqrt{9+4k})/2\). For \(k \ge -2\) the smaller root is \(\le 2\); it is extraneous when \(k > -2\) and equals 2 (valid) when \(k = -2\), giving two solutions.
So exactly one solution occurs for integer \(k = -1, 0, \dots, 10\) (12 values); \(k = -2\) gives two, and \(k \le -3\) gives none.
explanation.why: For k from -1 to 10 the larger root is valid and the smaller is extraneous; k = -2 keeps both, and k <= -3 has no real root.
explanation.pattern: After squaring, test each root in the original radical equation and track when the smaller root fails x - a >= 0.

items.stem: What is the sum of the squares of all real solutions to the equation \(\left||x - 3| - 5\right| = 1\)?

explanation.why: There are four solutions, 9, -3, 7 and -1, and their squares sum to 140.
explanation.pattern: Peel nested absolute values from the outside in, keeping both signs at each layer.

items.stem: The equations \(x^2 - 9x + 14 = 0\) and \(x^2 + kx - 7 = 0\), where \(k\) is a constant, have at least one solution in common. What is the product of all possible values of \(k\)?

steps: The first equation factors as \((x-2)(x-7) = 0\), so the only candidates for a common solution are 2 and 7.
The product is \((3/2)(-6) = -9\).
explanation.why: Each root of the first equation forces one value of k in the second, giving k = 3/2 and k = -6.
explanation.pattern: A shared solution must be a root of both equations; substitute each known root to solve for the parameter.

items.stem: The positive numbers \(x\) and \(y\) satisfy \(x^2 + xy = 40\) and \(y^2 + xy = 24\). What is the value of \(x - y\)?

steps: Adding the equations: \(x^2 + 2xy + y^2 = 64\), so \(x + y = 8\) since both are positive.
Factoring the first: \(x(x+y) = 40\), so \(x = 5\); then \(y = 3\).
Check the second: \(9 + 15 = 24\). So \(x - y = 2\).
explanation.why: The sum of the equations is (x+y)^2 = 64, which gives x = 5 and y = 3.
explanation.pattern: Add the equations to expose a perfect square, then factor each equation to separate the variables.

items.stem: The equation \(x^3 - 7x^2 + kx - 6 = 0\), where \(k\) is a constant, has \(x = 1\) as a solution. What is the sum of the squares of all three solutions of the equation?

steps: The solutions have sum \(7\) and pairwise-product sum \(12\).
Sum of squares \(= 7^2 - 2(12) = 25\) (the other two solutions are \(3 \pm \sqrt{3}\), whose squares sum to 24, plus \(1\)).
explanation.why: With k = 12, Vieta's formulas give 49 - 24 = 25.
explanation.pattern: Find the parameter from the known root, then use sum and pairwise-product relations instead of solving the cubic.

items.stem: In the xy-plane, the line \(y = 2x + 5\) intersects the circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 20\) at the two points \((x_1, y_1)\) and \((x_2, y_2)\). What is the value of \(x_1 + y_1 + x_2 + y_2\)?

steps: Substitute \(y = 2x + 5\): \(x^2 + (2x + 5)^2 = 20\), which simplifies to \(5x^2 + 20x + 5 = 0\), so \(x_1 + x_2 = -4\).
The total is \(-4 + 2 = -2\).
explanation.why: The intersection points are irrational, but only the sums are needed: the x-values sum to -4 (from the quadratic) and the y-values to 2 (from the line).
explanation.pattern: After substituting a line into a circle, use the sum of the roots (Vieta) and the line's equation instead of solving for each point.

items.stem: What is the solution to the equation \(3^{x + 2} + 3^{x - 1} = 252\)?

steps: Factor out the smaller power: \(3^{x-1}(3^3 + 1) = 252\), because \(3^{x+2} = 3^{x-1}\cdot 3^3\).
explanation.why: Writing both terms as multiples of 3^(x-1) turns the sum into 28 times one power, so 3^(x-1) = 9.
explanation.pattern: When exponential terms differ only by a shift in the exponent, factor out the smallest power instead of trying to take logarithms of a sum.

items.stem: The solutions to the equation \(2x^2 - 7x + 4 = 0\) are \(r\) and \(s\). Which of the following equations has solutions \(r^2\) and \(s^2\)?

choices.slip: Found the sum of the squares correctly but used the product rs = 2 instead of (rs)^2 = 4 for the product of the new roots.
Squared the sum of the roots (7/2)^2 = 49/4 and forgot to subtract 2rs, so the sum of the squares is wrong.
Subtracted rs = 2 instead of 2rs = 4 from (7/2)^2, giving 41/4 for the sum of the squares.

steps: The new equation is \(x^2 - \frac{33}{4}x + 4 = 0\); multiplying by 4 gives \(4x^2 - 33x + 16 = 0\).
explanation.why: New sum = (r+s)^2 - 2rs = 33/4 and new product = (rs)^2 = 4, so x^2 - (33/4)x + 4 = 0.
explanation.pattern: To build an equation whose roots are transformed roots, compute the new sum and product from r+s and rs, then write x^2 - (sum)x + (product).

items.stem: In the xy-plane, the circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 21\) and the parabola \(y = x^2 - 1\) intersect. What is the sum of the squares of the x-coordinates of all points of intersection?

steps: Since \(x^2 = y + 1\), the circle becomes \(y + 1 + y^2 = 21\), so \(y^2 + y - 20 = 0\) and \(y = 4\) or \(y = -5\).
The parabola has \(y \ge -1\) (because \(x^2 \ge 0\)), so \(y = -5\) gives \(x^2 = -4\), which is impossible. Only \(y = 4\) works.
Then \(x^2 = 5\), so the intersection points have \(x = \pm\sqrt{5}\), and the sum of the squares is \(5 + 5 = 10\).
explanation.why: Only y = 4 is possible on the parabola, giving two points with x^2 = 5 each; the root y = -5 is extraneous.
explanation.pattern: After eliminating x^2, check every solution against the range of the other curve before counting points.

items.stem: If \(2^x \cdot 4^y = 128\) and \(\dfrac{3^x}{9^y} = 27\), what is the value of \(xy\)?

steps: Write each side with a single base: \(2^{x + 2y} = 2^7\) and \(3^{x - 2y} = 3^3\).
So \(x + 2y = 7\) and \(x - 2y = 3\). Adding gives \(x = 5\), and then \(y = 1\).
explanation.pattern: Convert 4^y and 9^y to the bases 2 and 3 so each equation becomes a linear equation in the exponents.

items.stem: The graphs of \(xy = 18\) and \(y = -2x + m\), where \(m\) is a constant, intersect at exactly one point in the \(xy\)-plane. What is the product of all possible values of \(m\)?

steps: Exactly one intersection means the discriminant is zero: \(m^2 - 4(2)(18) = 0\), so \(m^2 = 144\) and \(m = 12\) or \(m = -12\).
The product is \(12 \cdot (-12) = -144\).
explanation.why: The line can touch the upper-right branch (m = 12) or the lower-left branch (m = -12), so both signs count; the product is negative, not 144.
explanation.pattern: A line meets a curve once when the substituted quadratic has discriminant zero; keep both signs of the resulting parameter.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 7x + 1\). What is the value of \(f(-3)\)?

choices.slip: Treated −7x at x = −3 as −21 instead of +21.
Squared −3 as −9 instead of 9.
Squared 2(−3) = −6 instead of squaring only the −3.

explanation.why: Squaring −3 gives +9, and subtracting a negative adds, so every term is positive: 18 + 21 + 1 = 40.
explanation.pattern: Put negative inputs in parentheses before squaring or multiplying; most wrong answers come from a lost sign.

items.stem: The value \(V(t)\), in dollars, of a used phone \(t\) years after it was bought is modeled by \(V(t) = 640(0.75)^t\). According to the model, what is the value of the phone, in dollars, \(2\) years after it was bought?

choices.slip: Took 25% of the original price off twice (a straight-line drop) instead of 25% of the current value each year.
This is the value after 1 year, not 2.
Multiplied by 0.75 × 2 = 1.5 instead of by 0.75 twice.

explanation.why: Each year the value is multiplied by 0.75, so after two years it is 640 × 0.75 × 0.75 = 360 dollars.
explanation.pattern: In a(b)^t, multiply by b once per time unit. Losing 25% twice is not losing 50%.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^2 + 6\). In the \(xy\)-plane, the graph of \(y = g(x)\) is the result of shifting the graph of \(y = f(x)\) down \(9\) units. Which equation defines \(g\)?

choices.slip: Shifted up 9 units instead of down.
Shifted right 9 units: changed the input instead of the output.
Shifted left 9 units: changed the input instead of the output.

steps: Shifting a graph down \(9\) units subtracts \(9\) from every output: \(g(x) = f(x) - 9\).
explanation.why: Moving down changes only the y-values, so 9 is subtracted outside the function: x² + 6 − 9 = x² − 3.
explanation.pattern: Up/down shifts change the outside (add or subtract after f); left/right shifts change the inside (x − h).

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^2 - 10x + c\), where \(c\) is a constant. The minimum value of \(f\) is \(7\). What is the value of \(c\)?

steps: For \(x^2 + bx + c\), the minimum occurs at \(x = -\frac{b}{2}\); here \(x = \frac{10}{2} = 5\).
The minimum value is \(f(5) = 25 - 50 + c = c - 25\).
explanation.why: With c = 32, f(x) = x² − 10x + 32 = (x − 5)² + 7, which is smallest (7) when x = 5.
explanation.pattern: The minimum value is the output at the vertex. Find the vertex x first, then plug it in.

items.stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, the graph of \(y = (x - 4)(x + 10)\) is a parabola with vertex \((h, k)\). What is the value of \(k\)?

steps: The \(x\)-intercepts are \(x = 4\) and \(x = -10\).
The vertex lies halfway between them: \(h = \frac{4 + (-10)}{2} = -3\).
explanation.why: The vertex sits at x = −3, midway between the roots 4 and −10, and the parabola's value there is (−7)(7) = −49.
explanation.pattern: Factored form gives the roots; average them for the vertex x, then plug that x back in for the vertex y.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = (x - 3)(x - k)\), where \(k\) is a constant and \(k > 3\). The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = f(x + 2)\). In the \(xy\)-plane, the graph of \(y = g(x)\) reaches its minimum at \(x = 4\). What is the minimum value of \(g\)?

steps: The graph of \(g(x) = f(x + 2)\) is the graph of \(f\) shifted left \(2\) units, so \(f\) reaches its minimum at \(x = 4 + 2 = 6\).
The vertex of \(f\) is halfway between its zeros \(3\) and \(k\): \(\frac{3 + k}{2} = 6\), so \(k = 9\).
A horizontal shift does not change the minimum value, so the minimum of \(g\) equals the minimum of \(f\): \(f(6) = (6 - 3)(6 - 9) = (3)(-3) = -9\).
explanation.why: f(x) = (x − 3)(x − 9) has its lowest point at (6, −9); shifting it 2 units left moves the lowest point to (4, −9) without changing its height.
explanation.pattern: f(x + c) moves the graph left c units and keeps the output values. Undo the shift to find the original vertex, then use the roots' midpoint.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = a(x - 3)^2 + k\), where \(a\) and \(k\) are constants. If \(f(1) = 11\) and \(f(6) = 31\), what is the value of \(f(3)\)?

explanation.why: At x = 3 the squared term is 0, so f(3) is just k, and the two given points pin k down to −5.
explanation.pattern: In vertex form, f(h) = k. Turn each given point into an equation in a and k, then eliminate a.

items.stem: A theater sells \(600\) tickets per show when the ticket price is \(\$20\). For each \(\$1\) increase in the price, it expects to sell \(15\) fewer tickets per show. Based on this, what ticket price, in dollars, would give the theater the greatest revenue per show? (Revenue is the price per ticket times the number of tickets sold.)

choices.slip: This is the best price increase x, not the ticket price.
This is the current price, before any increase.
At $60 (x = 40) revenue drops to 0; that is a zero of R, not the maximum.

steps: Let \(x\) be the price increase in dollars. The price is \(20 + x\) and the number sold is \(600 - 15x\), so revenue is \(R(x) = (20 + x)(600 - 15x)\).
The vertex is halfway between the zeros: \(x = \frac{-20 + 40}{2} = 10\).
The question asks for the price, not the increase: \(20 + 10 = 30\) dollars.
explanation.why: A $10 increase maximises revenue (30 × 450 = $13,500, more than at $29 or $31), and $20 + $10 = $30.
explanation.pattern: Build price × quantity from the story, use the zeros of the factored quadratic to find the vertex, and answer the quantity asked (price, not increase).

items.stem: The value of a machine, in dollars, \(t\) years after it is bought is modeled by \(V(t) = 8,000(0.64)^t\). According to the model, the value decreases by \(p\%\) every 6 months. What is the value of \(p\)?

steps: 6 months is \(\frac{1}{2}\) year, so every half year the value is multiplied by \((0.64)^{1/2}\).
Multiplying by 0.8 is a \(20\%\) decrease, so \(p = 20\).
explanation.why: Two half-year drops of 20% give 0.8 × 0.8 = 0.64, the yearly factor in the model, so the half-year drop is 20%.
explanation.pattern: To change the time unit of an exponential, raise the base to that fraction of the old unit. Halving 36% is a trap.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = a(b)^x\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are positive constants. If \(\frac{f(3)}{f(1)} = \frac{25}{4}\) and \(f(0) + f(2) = 29\), what is the value of \(f(1)\)?
